<span id="1ac0a8e1"></span>
# Event tracking planning

Before integrating the SDK, you need to perform event tracking planning based on your business analysis, and clarify which events and properties may require event tracking in the business indicators to be analyzed. When planning event tracking, you need to understand some basic concepts and pre\-information such as event tracking events and properties provided by DataFinder, DataFinder's user identity logic, etc., and combine the capabilities provided by DataFinder to plan event tracking.

<span id="0509e614"></span>
## Basic concept


|Basic concept |Concept note |Event tracking planning and SDK integration points |Detailed guidance document |
|---|---|---|---|
|Event, event property, event public property, user property |DataFinder's user behavior data analytics is based on event + user model.<br><br><br>* Event & Event property: One or a type of behavior of the user is called an "event". Event property is the information used to describe the event, such as the form and location of the event that are synchronously collected when the event is triggered. For example, if a user purchases a product, then the user's behavior event is "Purchase", and the event property is "Product Name" , "Product Classification", "Payment Amount", etc.<br><br>* Event public properties: Refers to **infrequently changing properties that** are not strongly associated with an event and are common to multiple or all events, such as the version number of the application, device information, etc.<br><br>* User & User property: User refers to the person who occurs the event behavior. User properties refer to properties of the user's own state (independent of behavior, such as age, gender, etc.) or user\-related properties (such as VIP level, registration time, etc.) that are related to behavior but do not change frequently. |You need to plan the events, event properties, and user properties to be collected according to the needs of business analysis. When integrating the SDK |Please see the detailed concept introduction [Data Model](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Data_Model). |
|Event tracking, full event tracking, custom event tracking |* Event tracking: Through the development of the SDK, the process of writing event logic into the code is called **event tracking**. DataFinder provides you with preset events and event properties that do not require manual event tracking, just turn on the capture switch .<br><br>* Full event tracking: is a kind of preset events and event properties provided by DataFinder. In DataFinder, the full event tracking events collected are bav2b_click button clicks and bav2b_page page browsing. No additional investment in research and development is required, but it will be at the expense of reporting a large amount of data, and only simple PV and UV can be collected, which is a bit'powerless' for the collection of rich business data.<br><br>* Code event tracking: Code event tracking refers to the development engineer who manually writes the code to implement the data collection logic according to the personalized needs of the business. Wide collection range and flexible application. However, it requires investment in research and development and requires certain technical capabilities. |It is usually recommended that you combine the preset events/properties and custom event tracking provided by DataFinder for event tracking planning. |[Event Tracking, Full Event Tracking](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Event_Tracking_Full_Event_Tracking) |


<span id="5d6c3cec"></span>
## Understanding data reporting requirements (format, quantity restrictions, etc.)

When planning for event tracking, you need to be clear about the data format requirements of the events and properties to be collected and reported, as well as some restrictions on collection and reporting, so as to avoid subsequent failure to meet the requirements due to data formats, which will lead to data collection that cannot be warehoused and cannot be queried and analyzed later.

The data reported by the SDK usually has a fixed format, including headers and events.


|Field |Effect |Data example |
|---|---|---|
|header |Store event public property.<br><br>app_id, os_name These are preset and will be placed directly under the header. If it is the event public property you customize, it will be placed under header.custom. |For details, please refer to the data structure reported by the corresponding native SDK. |
|event |Store events and event properties.<br><br>Events are divided into launch, terminate, event_v3.<br><br>The launch and terminate are preset start and exit events.<br><br>event_v3 store custom event, page event, etc., each event_v3 type event has event, params, local_time_ms, session_id fields, among which local_time_ms, session_id are automatically generated by the SDK, and event, params are business settings, event is the event name, params store is the event property (the value is a JSON object serialized operation). ||


Among them, when you need to report custom events and custom properties, you need to ensure that the data format of the event and property meets the requirements. Please refer to the data format requirements and data reporting restrictions supported by the current DataFinder [Supported Data Formats and Event/Property Classification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification).

Common problem:


* Event property data type transmission error, need to modify how to do?[Q1: Event property data type transmission error, how to modify?](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification#q1%EF%BC%9A%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6%E5%B1%9E%E6%80%A7%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E7%B1%BB%E5%9E%8B%E4%BC%A0%E8%BE%93%E9%94%99%E8%AF%AF%EF%BC%8C%E9%9C%80%E8%A6%81%E4%BF%AE%E6%94%B9%E6%80%8E%E4%B9%88%E5%8A%9E%EF%BC%9F)

* The data type transmission at each end is inconsistent. How does the system handle it? How to modify?[Q2: The data type transmission at each end is inconsistent. How does the system handle it? How to modify it?](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification#q2%EF%BC%9A-%E5%90%84%E7%AB%AF%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E7%B1%BB%E5%9E%8B%E4%BC%A0%E8%BE%93%E4%B8%8D%E4%B8%80%E8%87%B4%EF%BC%8C%E7%B3%BB%E7%BB%9F%E5%A6%82%E4%BD%95%E5%A4%84%E7%90%86%EF%BC%9F%E5%A6%82%E4%BD%95%E4%BF%AE%E6%94%B9%EF%BC%9F)


<span id="bcfc227a"></span>
## Understanding user identity logic

When planning for event tracking, you need to understand the user identity logic of DataFinder, which is used to combine the user identity logic of your own business to eventually unify the source of user identity data. DataFinder defaults to the **user** as the object of statistical analysis, and uses SSID as the user's unique identification ID to calculate the indicator. At this time, the user's SSID is the default statistical criteria. When your analysis object is a user, it is recommended to keep the default statistical criteria SSID. DataFinder can restore a real user individual through an SSID ID_Mapping after mapping the user's device_id, user_unique_id, etc.


* **device_id:**  It can be used as the unique ID of the device, which is mostly used in scenarios where the user's real\-name ID cannot be obtained.

* **user_unique_id:**  It is the login user ID, which is mostly used in the scenario where the user's real\-name ID can be obtained. Generally, the user ID used in the product business is directly used, such as the login account. When the user_unique_id is not set, in the SaaS version, the system will automatically use device_id replacement.

* **SSID:**  DataFinder user statistics criteria ID, with the device identification device_id, login state user identification user_unique_id mutual Mapping, can ensure the user anonymity and real\-name status of the ID unity.


See the mapping logic for the three types of IDs and more information about user identities [Supported User Unique Identifiers](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_User_Unique_Identifiers).

<span id="d08d4669"></span>
## Understand client side supported preset events and properties

As mentioned above, in most business analysis scenarios, you need to combine your own business characteristics for custom event tracking planning and integration. Before that, you can first understand the preset events and preset properties currently provided by DataFinder, and combine the existing preset events and property capabilities to further plan the requirements for custom code event tracking.


* See the list of preset events and properties supported by the app [Android-Side Preset Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Android-Side_Preset_Events_and_Properties).

* At the same time, you also need to pay attention to the list of currently disabled preset properties. When planning custom event tracking and properties in the future, you need to avoid the same name as the disabled properties, otherwise the data will not be reported normally. See for details [Disable Properties List](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Disable_Properties_List).

# Preparation

<span id="48fb01f4"></span>
## Step 1 (optional): Create event tracking requirements/Enter custom event tracking

After completing the event tracking planning, it is recommended that you create the event tracking requirements according to the planning and then enter the custom event tracking into the DataFinder to complete the warehousing of the custom event tracking in the DataFinder metadata.


* Event tracking request management: You can manage event tracking requirements through DataFinder's event tracking request management function, and you can continue to maintain and manage requirements in the event tracking request management page to improve management efficiency. See the operation to create event tracking request management [Request Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Request_Management).

* Custom event tracking entry: You can first create custom event tracking metadata into the DataFinder according to the event tracking plan. For activity details, see [New event](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Events#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6), [Add event properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Event_Properties#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6%E5%B1%9E%E6%80%A7), [Add user properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/User_Properties#533b53ea).

## Step1: Adding Flutter plugins and native dependencies

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">Capturing essentially relies on the capturing capabilities of the native SDK. The Flutter plugin is just an implementation of the Method Channel, which is used to call the API of the native SDK, so you need to add both the Flutter plugin and the native dependencies.</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">Currently, the Flutter plugin <code>rangers_applog_flutter_plugin</code>the latest version <code>1.5.0</code>and supports the Flutter platform version 3.x.</div>


Using the Flutter plugin and native dependencies, here's how:

<span id="c45a036d"></span>
### Add Flutter plugin


1. Add `rangers_applog_flutter_plugin`dependencies in `pubspec.yaml`for Flutter project

   ```YAML
   dependencies:
     # ...
     rangers_applog_flutter_plugin: 1.5.0
   ```
   

2. Perform the installation

   ```Shell
   flutter packages get
   ```

<span id="90b65699"></span>
### Reporting customs events

According to the event tracking plan, if you need to collect and report custom events, you can use "onEventV3" to set the custom event name and event properties.


|Operation guidance |
|---|
|```Dart```<br>```import 'package:rangers_applog_flutter_plugin/rangers_applog_flutter_plugin.dart';```<br>``````<br>```//Example: Report event event_name , the event does not contain property```<br>```RangersApplogFlutterPlugin.onEventV3("event_name");```<br>``````<br>```//Example: Report event event_name with two properties```<br>```A property of type string with the property name key_string and the property value value_string```<br>```//A property of type int, the property name is key_int, and the property value is 10```<br>```RangersApplogFlutterPlugin.onEventV3("event_name", {```<br>```    "key_string": "value_string",```<br>```    "key_int": 10```<br>```});```<br> |


<span id="e0227398"></span>
### Set user login status

If you need to set user login status, you can use the setUserUniqueId method to set user_unique_id property.

Usually, when a user needs to log in with a real name, the business will use an ID to uniquely identify the user. You can report the user ID of the corresponding business through the setUserUniqueId method. Usually this value can be obtained through the service interface, or directly read the existing fixed user ID value. If you need to understand the DataFinder's user identity logic, see [Supported User Unique Identifiers](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_User_Unique_Identifiers).


|Operation guidance |
|---|
|```Dart```<br>```import 'package:rangers_applog_flutter_plugin/rangers_applog_flutter_plugin.dart';```<br>``````<br>```//Set the ID of your account system when logging in and ensure its uniqueness```<br>```RangersApplogFlutterPlugin.setUserUniqueId('{{USER_UNIQUE_ID}}');```<br> |

<span id="d43c7714"></span>
## Event tracking data validation

After completing the initialization verification, you can perform test operations on the client side to trigger some events to be collected and reported. After the test event is reported, within about 15 minutes, you can view the specific user behavior flow data on the `user scrutiny`page in the `growth analysis platform`, that is, you can see the test event and event property data, which is used to verify whether the event tracking data can be collected and reported normally.


* The user behavior stream data displayed in the user scrutiny page usually has a fixed format, mainly including `user`, `header`, `events`three parts, which respectively display the user property data collected and reported, public event property property, event and event property data. The reported data contains preset and custom data that are opened for collection.

* If the corresponding event can be seen in the user's investigation, indicating that the event was successfully reported, by observing the property of the event, it can be confirmed whether the corresponding property was also successfully reported.

* If the data is not found in the user scrutiny normally, you can check it:

   * Whether the data format of the reported data meets the requirements: [Supported Data Formats and Event/Property Classification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification).

   * Check that the AppID in the integration code is correct [Import and initialize](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Mini_Program_SDK_Integration#eaa78476).

   * For SaaS\-cloud native and privatized environments, check whether the reported domain name in the integration code is configured correctly: [Examples of domain name reporting for each environment](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_Integration#532f6155).

# SDK API List

DataFinder provides you with rich API interfaces. In addition to the core interfaces and typical scenarios described in the above general process, you can also understand the main API interfaces supported by the current iOS and their functions. According to business needs, you can flexibly call the corresponding interface to complete the business tracking event.


|Classification |API List |API Description |
|---|---|---|
|main API |[initRangersAppLog](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#d7a3a62d) |Initialize the SDK |
||[addInitParams](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#068d02d5) |Support to add some additional initialization settings, currently supports `region`, `autoStart`, `service_vendor`three settings. This method needs to be executed before initRangersAppLog |
||[start](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#4c0d7a3c) |When autoStart is set to false through addInitParams, you need to actively call the start method to inform the SDK to start reporting events |
||[setUserUniqueId](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#99937276) |Set the user login state, set the user_unique_id value after initialization, and the SDK will save it, so it only needs to be set when the change occurs |
||[onEventV3](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#b2d173ef) |Report the event and set it after initialization before calling it. |
||[setHeaderInfo](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#c939db2b) |Set custom public properties |
||[removeHeaderInfo](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#237d27fa) |Remove custom public properties |
||[getDeviceId](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#d8bb9e74) |Get platform ID |
|Module API |[AB test API Description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#0daa2e24) |The SDK provides AB test capabilities and provides a series of methods: getAbSdkVersion, getAllAbTestConfig, getABTestConfigValueForKey |
||[User Attributes Features API Description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Flutter_SDK_API_Description#86c82366) |Provides the ability to set user properties and provides a series of methods: profileSet, profileSetOnce, profileUnset, profileIncrement, profileAppend |
